newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Greece agrees to speed up telecoms liberalisation.
newsitem.headline: Greece agrees to speed up telecoms liberalisation.

text.p: The Greek government has agreed to take a series of steps to speed up liberalisation of its telecommunications market, the European Commission said on Wednesday.

In a meeting with Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert on Tuesday, Greek Telecoms Minister Charis Kastanides agreed that his government would take action on satellite communications, cable TV networks, leased lines and the national regulatory authority.
The Commission said in a statement that it welcomed the pledges, but would continue its plan to take legal action if they were not fulfilled.
The Commission said it would decide shortly whether to grant Greece's request for a five-year extension to the EU's January 1, 1998 deadline for abolishing all state telecoms monopolies.
It said in a statement Greece had agreed to:
-- Implement EU rules on competition in satellite communications by August 1, while allowing licence applications to be reviewed immediately.
-- Amend a law that gives state phone company OTE a monopoly over cable TV infrastructure within 12 months.
-- Allow operaters other than OTE to apply for DCS 1800 mobile communications licences and to set licence fees in a non-discriminatory way.
-- Implement by August staff regulations that will allow its independent telecoms regulatory authority to become fully operational.
-- Implement by the end of the year EU rules requiring state phone companies to lease lines at cost-oriented tariffs.
Greece has asked to wait until January 1, 2003 to fully liberalise its telecoms market -- a move allowed under EU law -- on the grounds that OTE needs more time to complete a modernisation project.
